findings.source_quote: Ἄκουε, φησίν, ἀμφοτέρων τὴν δύναμιν, [τῆς τρυφῆς καὶ τῆς βασάνου].
findings.english_quote: “Hear,” he says, “the force of both indulgence and torment.”
findings.issue: The English incorporates the bracketed editorial supplement identifying the two things as indulgence and torment without disclosing its status. Neither footnote explains these brackets. The supplied working-source report explicitly retains this critical marking; the edition therefore fails to distinguish the supplement from preserved wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the source-compatible rendering, but add a note attached to “indulgence and torment” explaining that these identifying words are bracketed as an editorial supplement in the selected working Greek. Any proposed note requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Ἄκουε, φησίν, ἀμφοτέρων τὴν δύναμιν, [τῆς τρυφῆς καὶ τῆς βασάνου].
findings.english_quote: He says, “Hear the force of both indulgence and torment.”
findings.issue: Independently compared with the Greek, the simplified edition also presents the bracketed identification “indulgence and torment” without identifying it as an editorial supplement. Its retained notes explain the paragraph 2 selection and the numerical comparisons, but not this source distinction.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the source-compatible wording and add an accessible note explaining that “indulgence and torment” is an editorial supplement shown in brackets in the selected working Greek. Submit the proposed note for fresh review.

summary: Both editions preserve the passage’s substantive clauses, speaker distinctions, negations, sevenfold proposal, and difficult hour/day/year comparisons. The contextual rendering “Sir” is documented. The paragraph 2 note accurately discloses the bounded, edition-mediated Lavra selection and the older conjectural alternative; no replacement of that working reading is warranted. Both editions need disclosure of the paragraph 3 editorial supplement. This review assesses the supplied Greek and attributed reports, not unseen manuscript images, edition authentication, or exhaustive witness collation.
